On the bridge we ran quick diagnostics. Initial findings and immediate mitigations: 

Findings (first-pass):
- Node-level telemetry shows persistent KV-cache thrashing on shard group g4-32-08 and elevated coroutine queue depth on the inference runtime for Treadstone's reserved workers.
- Two adjacent tenants on the same node increased sequence length unexpectedly (longer prompts) which pushed kernel selection to a slower path and amplified token compute time (noisy neighbor effect).
- Autoscaler did not react in time due to a config anomaly in the reserved-pool policy; scale-up triggered but only after 9 minutes.

Immediate mitigations applied (complete within 20-30 min):
1) Disabled lower-priority tenants on g4-32-08 (moved to hosted overflow).
2) Manually triggered scale-up on the reserved pool and pinned faster kernel variant for Treadstone model version v3.1.
3) Restarted the inference worker process on g4-32-08 to clear the KV cache; warming in-progress.
4) Temporarily bumped KV cache TTL and reduced max sequence fallback to limit thrash.

ETA: we expect throughput to approach normal within ~45 minutes; we'll watch 5xx rate and 95th latency.

Follow-ups (next 2 hours):
- Root cause postmortem (includes autoscaler rule fix)
- Engineering change to prevent cross-tenant kernel fallbacks in reserved pools

I'll post live metrics and a short incident_timeline_stub.md (attached) once we've validated.

-David
